payload.name: Resolve Weekday Event Dates in Memories
payload.description: When extracting or adding an event memory, if a message reports an event with a relative time phrase like 'On Friday' or 'yesterday' and the message has a timestamp, resolve that phrase to a concrete calendar date and include the date in the memory content.
content: During extraction, when a speaker reports a past event using a weekday or other relative time phrase (e.g., 'On Friday', 'last week', 'yesterday'), compute the exact calendar date from the message timestamp and include that date in the memory content, not just in future-planning fields.
During CRUD, when adding or updating such an event memory, preserve the resolved date in the memory content and set world_start to it if the date is the event's occurrence time.

Stop after resolving the one date the phrase refers to; do not invent or expand to additional dates unless the source explicitly provides them, and do not apply this to relative phrases that only describe future plans rather than the event's occurrence.

solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops an event's concrete date when it is stated only as a weekday/relative phrase (e.g., 'On Friday'), making later date questions unanswerable. This Skill applies when a timestamped message reports an event with such a phrase; resolve it to the exact calendar date and store it in the event memory. It does not apply when the message already has an explicit date or when the phrase only describes a future plan.
